outlook.statement: Rising consumption, growing demand for hygiene and tissue products, increasing environmental awareness and the shift towards sustainable packaging solutions are expected to support industry growth. The company remains confident of the medium and long-term prospects of the paper industry.

While new industry capacity additions may create short-term headwinds in the tissue market, robust demand growth will support long-term value creation. The company's diversified product portfolio and broad market presence position it well to capitalize on opportunities while sustaining long-term profitable growth.

The business has begun responding positively to the structural interventions implemented across operations, products, and organisational culture. Priorities remain: increasing contribution of value-added products, expanding manufacturing capacity, improving profitability, reducing fixed costs, optimising working capital, and lowering dependence on commoditized segments.

Focus will remain on strengthening talent, enhancing capabilities and enabling transformation for a future-ready organization; greatest competitive advantage lies in collective potential of its people.
Tissue-4 machine expected to be fully operational by September 2028.

Company plans to progressively implement projects with longer payback periods under Project Urja Mitra, unlocking additional savings and reinforcing commitment to operational excellence and sustainable manufacturing.

Capex project for installing a new Tissue line has been initiated. This capital infusion shall bring in state-of-art technology to Orient Paper and help it stay relevant in today's markets by expanding its product basket and improving its profitability. This shall de-commoditize the Company's product mix and shift it towards value-added categories.
The Company remains steadfast in its commitment of achieving net neutrality targets in both carbon and water footprints.

Indian paper industry volume growth estimated at ~5-6% during CY2024-26, driven by favorable demographics, rising literacy, increasing packaging demand, and shift towards organized and value-added segments. Tissue paper market experiencing strong growth of 10-15%. Caustic soda demand expected to sustain at CAGR ~6-7%.

Company initiated capex project for installing a new Tissue line with state-of-art technology to expand product basket, improve profitability, and de-commoditize product mix towards value-added categories.

Company remains committed to achieving net neutrality targets in both carbon and water footprints. Expanded plantation coverage by 16,491 acres in FY26. Proportion of renewables in energy mix maintained at ~40%.

Investment risk: The defined benefit plans are funded with insurance companies of India. The Company does not have any liberty to manage the funds provided to insurance companies. If the return on plan asset is below the discount rate, it will create a plan deficit.

Discount rate risk: The Company is exposed to the risk of fall in discount rate. A fall in discount rate will eventually increase the ultimate cost of providing the above benefit thereby increasing the value of the liability.
Demographic risk: The Company is exposed to this risk to the extent of actual experience eventually being worse compared to the assumptions thereby causing an increase in the benefit cost.
Salary growth risk: An increase in the salary of the plan participants will increase the plan liability.
